analysis:
This batch changes only CI test files (.github/scripts/test-threat-bedrock.py and metadata for test-threat-budget.py), none of which is provider, coordinator or native-runtime code in the canonical threat model. I found no change to the in-scope assets (A-001 to A-017) or trust boundaries (TB-002, TB-003, TB-007, TB-009, TB-010, TB-011). The T-041 prefix-cache definition is not touched.

The test changes encode tighter CI review-tool behavior:
- Missing or invalid Bedrock usage now preserves the response text, records unknown usage and permanently stops later requests with BEDROCK_USAGE_MISSING or BEDROCK_USAGE_RECORD_FAILED.
- Fallback is never used in these cases.
- Response validation still rejects invalid JSON and truncated output.
- The integration-stage schema now restricts covered_units to an enum of unit IDs.
- The merge gate tests require a result 'run' field matching GITHUB_RUN_ID and GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT, so stale or unattributed reports cannot clear a PR.

These are test-only changes. Whether the production code (threat_review/bedrock.py, review.py, threat-review-gate.py) actually implements them is not in the supplied evidence, so that is an unverified contract for integration, not a finding. Unit 55758f70f3239290:0 supplied metadata only. Its patch excerpt shows test-only edits such as a larger server backlog and the WRITE_ATTEMPTS constant, and I saw no security-relevant concern.

No provider-facing attack surface, secret handling or threat-model gap was introduced by the supplied lines.
